Neville believes United have handled the situation poorly, with Carrick taking training in Manchester while club executives met in Monaco on Wednesday and pursued Pochettino as his replacement .

items.title: Could King really become 'one of the best players in the world'?
items.excerpt: Josh King was always one of the best players in his age group. "Nationally," clarifies Charlie Turnbull, his coach in Fulham's academy for five seasons between his U10 and U14 years, to Sky Sports . But there was another quality that set hi…
body: Josh King was always one of the best players in his age group. "Nationally," clarifies Charlie Turnbull, his coach in Fulham's academy for five seasons between his U10 and U14 years, to Sky Sports . But there was another quality that set him apart.

"One of the most outstanding things about Josh is that whenever the level went up, whenever there was a pressure game, he loved it," adds Turnbull. "He loved it when things got hard. He loved it when there was a little bit of extra pressure.

"He wanted it. He wanted to feel like the pressure was on him and the responsibility was on him to produce for the team. He enjoyed that. You always saw the best of Josh when the ante was up. I never once saw him not deliver in those circumstances.

"We would play tournaments in France, Spain and Portugal, against the giants of Europe, and afterwards the staff from each club would have to pick the best player they'd seen across the weekend. I remember Josh winning that accolade more than once."

items.title: Kane targets biggest team prizes ahead of record-breaking England cap
items.excerpt: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
body: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world.

But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

"To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," he said in a press conference on Wednesday when asked what comes next for him. "That's always been my biggest dream, to win a European Championship or a World Cup, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is. Extremely motivated to do that.
